abstract:
The direct comparisons between transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) and Yttrium-90 (Y-90) radioembolization in combination with systemic therapies to treat unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are lacking, and the distinct impacts of these combination therapies on the tumor microenvironment (TME) have not been investigated. The aim of this study was to directly compare the clinical efficacy and post-treatment TME profiles between TACE and Y-90 plus systemic therapies.
A total of 210 patients with unresectable HCC were included and divided into 2 groups: TACE + systemic therapies (n = 159) and Y-90 + systemic therapies (n = 51). Baseline characteristics and clinical outcomes between these 2 groups were compared. Furthermore, TME profiles after TACE + systemic therapies and Y-90 + systemic therapies were analyzed by single-cell RNA sequencing. Besides, the multiplex immunofluorescence was conducted to verify these TME characteristics.
Y-90 + systemic therapies group showed significantly higher disease control rate and conversion rate compared to TACE + systemic therapies group (p < 0.05). Also, Y-90 + systemic therapies showed higher progression-free survival and overall survival compared to TACE + systemic therapies (p < 0.05). Notably, single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that Y-90 + systemic therapies was associated with a more immune-activated TME, characterized by reduced T cell exhaustion, a lower proportion of regulatory T cells and enrichment of immune activation and chemotaxis pathways.
Y-90 + systemic therapies was associated with favorable clinical outcomes and distinct post-treatment tumor microenvironment characteristics. These findings provide exploratory insights into potential biological differences between Y-90 and TACE-based combination strategies.
